note: Non-laronidase IDUA delivery: lentiviral HSC (azamidugene autotemcel), intracisternal AAV9 (RGX-111), liver ZFN editing (devafidugene civaparvovec, failed) and BBB-crossing valanafusp alfa; all phase 1/2 or ongoing phase 3.
label: MPS I (IDUA gene/enzyme delivery)

engagement.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
engagement.note: Lentiviral HSC gene therapy gave supranormal blood IDUA and corrected GAG storage in Idua-/- mice; no patients yet.
engagement.quote: Interestingly, therapeutic efficacy of HSC gene therapy is strictly dependent on the achievement of supranormal enzyme activity in the hematopoietic system of transplanted mice, which allows enzyme delivery to the brain and skeleton for disease correction.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the OTL-203 (azamidugene autotemcel) parent model; same San Raffaele group and vector design.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Surrogate molecule: valanafusp's HIR antibody does not bind mouse receptor.
engagement.note: Surrogate murine TfR antibody-IDUA fusion cleared peripheral GAG and cut brain inclusions 73% in MPS I mice.
engagement.quote: Treatment of the MPSI mice with the cTfRMAb-IDUA reduced intracellular lysosomal inclusion bodies by 73% in brain, as compared to the MPSI mice treated with saline.
engagement.judgement: Valanafusp alfa cannot be tested in mice (primate-specific insulin receptor), so the disease model used a mouse-TfR sibling fusion: product_in_model false.

engagement.model: MPS I cat and dog, intrathecal/intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA
engagement.note: Intrathecal AAV9-IDUA virtually corrected CNS storage in MPS I cats; dog work followed.
engagement.quote: Treated animals demonstrated virtually complete correction of biochemical and histological manifestations of the disease throughout the CNS.
engagement.judgement: Penn group whose vector became RGX-111 (AAV9.CB7.hIDUA); treated as the RGX-111 parent model.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Quote is the first 37 words of a longer sentence.
engagement.model: Idua-/- mouse, ZFN albumin-locus IDUA insertion
engagement.note: ZFN insertion of IDUA at the albumin locus gave sustained liver-secreted IDUA and GAG correction in MPS I mice.
engagement.quote: A corrective copy of the IDUA gene is inserted at the albumin locus in hepatocytes, leading to sustained enzyme expression, secretion from the liver into circulation, and subsequent uptake systemically at levels sufficient for correction of metabolic disease
engagement.judgement: Sangamo's proof-of-concept for SB-318 (devafidugene civaparvovec), published after the 2017 first dosing; it was the stated basis, not a retrodiction.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; uncontrolled before-after comparison. Brain enzyme uptake was not measured in patients.
engagement.note: Urinary GAG stabilized or improved over 52 weeks of weekly valanafusp in 11 children, as the surrogate predicted for peripheral storage.
engagement.quote: Somatic manifestations were stabilized, or improved, based on urinary glycosaminoglycan levels, hepatic and spleen volumes, and shoulder range of motion.
engagement.reason: Urine GAG fell as in mice
engagement.judgement: Paired by me with the surrogate mouse study. Only the peripheral readout has a human counterpart; brain inclusion bodies do not. Substrate GAG read as proximal.

engagement.magnitude_basis: blood IDUA activity, supranormal vs supranormal
engagement.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
engagement.note: All eight Hurler children reached supraphysiologic blood IDUA within a month, sustained, as the mouse required.
engagement.short: Supraphysiologic blood IDUA in all patients
engagement.quote: All the patients showed prompt and sustained engraftment of gene-corrected cells and had supraphysiologic blood IDUA activity within a month, which was maintained up to the latest follow-up.
engagement.reason: Blood IDUA supranormal as in mice
engagement.judgement: Paired by me with Visigalli 2010. Blood IDUA is the transgene's own product, so proximal.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CSF heparan sulfate / CNS GAG decrease
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor press release (WORLDSymposium 2022); the 2026 single-patient paper (Wang 2026) also reports CSF data. No registry results posted for NCT03580083.
engagement.model: MPS I cat and dog, intrathecal/intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA
engagement.note: CSF heparan sulfate fell in all four evaluable RGX-111 patients; CSF IDUA became detectable in three.
engagement.short: CSF HS fell, CSF IDUA detected
engagement.quote: In the Phase I/II trial, a decrease in HS in the CSF from baseline was observed through the last timepoint available in all four patients following administration of RGX-111.
engagement.reason: CSF substrate fell as in cats
engagement.judgement: Tier 5 patient side, model side Hinderer 2014. CSF HS is the enzyme's substrate, read as proximal like the cat CNS GAG readout.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sustained plasma/leukocyte IDUA: supraphysiologic in mice vs none sustained in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry results posted 2023-01-26 (NCT02702115): leukocyte IDUA change -1.2 (cohort 1) and -2.5 (cohort 2).
engagement.model: Idua-/- mouse, ZFN albumin-locus IDUA insertion
engagement.note: Editing detected in liver but no sustained IDUA in blood; leukocyte IDUA rose only transiently in MPS I subjects.
engagement.quote: Overall, ZFN in vivo editing therapy had a favorable safety profile with evidence of targeted genome editing in liver, but no long-term enzyme expression in blood.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me with Ou 2018. The mouse's core claim was sustained enzyme expression; patients had none, so contra.

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC author manuscript via Firecrawl).
engagement.quote: IDUA activity in CSF rapidly increased following vector administration, exceeding that of normal controls by day 7
engagement.note: Intracisternal clinical-candidate AAV9-hIDUA raised CSF IDUA above normal and normalized CSF hexosaminidase in tolerized MPS I dogs.
engagement.short: CSF IDUA up, CSF Hex normalized
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the draft's cat model: different species, tolerized to human IDUA, and the vector named the clinical candidate.
engagement.model: MPS I dogs tolerized to human IDUA, intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA (clinical candidate vector)

engagement.magnitude_basis: CSF heparan sulfate change from baseline (4/4 decreased); CSF IDUA detectable in 3/4
engagement.confidence_note: Patient side is a sponsor press release (tier 5); no peer-reviewed RGX-111 results found. Scraped verbatim.
engagement.quote: In the Phase I/II trial, a decrease in HS in the CSF from baseline was observed through the last timepoint available in all four patients following administration of RGX-111.
engagement.note: CSF heparan sulfate fell in all four evaluable RGX-111 patients and CSF IDUA became detectable in three, as the dogs predicted.
engagement.judgement: Pairing: the dog paper proposed CSF IDUA as the clinical readout; press release reports CSF HS and IDUA, not a stated comparison.
engagement.model: MPS I dogs tolerized to human IDUA, intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA (clinical candidate vector)

engagement.quote: The HIRMAb-IDUA fusion protein bound with high affinity to the HIR, and was rapidly transported into the brain of the adult Rhesus monkey following intravenous administration.
engagement.note: Primate brain uptake of the fusion protein (1.2% ID/brain in Boado 2017); patient CSF HS/DS was a registered secondary of NCT03071341 with no posted result.
engagement.judgement: Giugliani 2018 reports urinary GAG, DQ and grey matter volume, not CSF HS/DS; brain delivery itself was never measured in patients.
engagement.model: Rhesus monkey brain uptake of IV HIRMAb-IDUA (valanafusp) vs recombinant IDUA

engagement.quote: Overall, the results obtained in these studies provided robust evidence to support the safety and tolerability of high-efficiency LV-mediated gene transfer and above-normal IDUA enzyme expression in both murine and human HSPCs and their in vivo progeny.
engagement.note: Human HSPCs, including patients' cells, transduced with the clinical vector gave above-normal IDUA in their in vivo progeny in xenografts.
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the draft's Idua-/- mouse: the system is human HSPCs in immunodeficient mice.
engagement.model: NSG mice engrafted with human (incl. MPS I patient) HSPCs transduced with clinical-grade IDUA lentiviral vector; GLP tox/biodistribution

engagement.magnitude_basis: blood IDUA activity relative to normal
engagement.quote: All the patients showed prompt and sustained engraftment of gene-corrected cells and had supraphysiologic blood IDUA activity within a month, which was maintained up to the latest follow-up.
engagement.note: All eight Hurler children engrafted and reached supraphysiologic blood IDUA, as human-cell xenografts predicted.
engagement.judgement: Pairing of the GLP xenograft paper with the trial; the NEJM abstract does not state the comparison.
engagement.model: NSG mice engrafted with human (incl. MPS I patient) HSPCs transduced with clinical-grade IDUA lentiviral vector; GLP tox/biodistribution

dose.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
dose.note: Mouse study stated that supranormal hematopoietic IDUA is required for brain and skeletal correction.
dose.quote: Interestingly, therapeutic efficacy of HSC gene therapy is strictly dependent on the achievement of supranormal enzyme activity in the hematopoietic system of transplanted mice, which allows enzyme delivery to the brain and skeleton for disease correction.
dose.judgement: The model's stated exposure target is supranormal hematopoietic IDUA activity.

dose.magnitude_basis: blood IDUA activity relative to normal, supranormal in both
dose.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
dose.note: Supraphysiologic blood IDUA reached within a month in all eight children and sustained.
dose.quote: All the patients showed prompt and sustained engraftment of gene-corrected cells and had supraphysiologic blood IDUA activity within a month, which was maintained up to the latest follow-up.
dose.judgement: Paired by me. The trial's co-primary end point (correction of blood IDUA up to supraphysiologic levels) is the mouse target; it was reached, so dose same. Whether it worked is efficacy.

dose.model: Rhesus monkey PK and chronic toxicology, AGT-181
dose.note: Repeat IV AGT-181 0.2-20 mg/kg in rhesus caused no toxicity and no glucose change.
dose.quote: Chronic AGT-181 dosing resulted in no toxicity at any dose, no changes in organ histology, no change in plasma or cerebrospinal fluid glucose, and no significant immune response.
dose.judgement: Stated tolerability margin; product_in_model true (AGT-181 is valanafusp alfa). Not a disease model.

dose.magnitude_basis: highest tolerated weekly dose, 6 mg/kg human vs 30 mg/kg monkey hypoglycemia threshold
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; whether infusions carried dextrose as the monkey study advised was not confirmed from the abstract.
dose.model: Rhesus monkey PK and chronic toxicology, AGT-181
dose.note: Children dosed weekly to 6 mg/kg, below the 30 mg/kg monkey hypoglycemia dose, completed 52 weeks; hypoglycemia transient.
dose.quote: Drug related adverse events included infusion related reactions, with an incidence of 1.7%, and transient hypoglycemia, with an incidence of 6.4%.
dose.judgement: Paired by me with Boado 2009/2012. Margin held in that dosing reached 6 mg/kg without being stopped; the hypoglycemia itself is counted once, in safety.

dose.quote: These studies established the efficacy of the human vector in the canine model, and allowed for estimation of the minimum effective dose, providing key information for the design of first-in-human trials.
dose.note: Dog study estimated a minimum effective intracisternal dose for first-in-human design; no published mapping to the 1e10-5e10 GC/g brain human cohorts.
dose.judgement: Human cohorts are dosed per gram brain mass; converting the dog GC/kg doses would be my own arithmetic, which the brief excludes.
dose.model: MPS I dogs tolerized to human IDUA, intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA (clinical candidate vector)

efficacy.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
efficacy.note: Mouse HSC gene therapy fully corrected MPS I, beating HSCT on brain and skeleton.
efficacy.quote: Interestingly, therapeutic efficacy of HSC gene therapy is strictly dependent on the achievement of supranormal enzyme activity in the hematopoietic system of transplanted mice, which allows enzyme delivery to the brain and skeleton for disease correction.

efficacy.note: Surrogate fusion cleared organ GAG and reversed brain storage in adult MPS I mice.
efficacy.quote: Treatment of the MPSI mice with the cTfRMAb-IDUA reduced intracellular lysosomal inclusion bodies by 73% in brain, as compared to the MPSI mice treated with saline.

efficacy.model: MPS I cat and dog, intrathecal/intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA
efficacy.note: Cat model corrected biochemically; it has no defined neurological phenotype.
efficacy.quote: Treated animals demonstrated virtually complete correction of biochemical and histological manifestations of the disease throughout the CNS.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the RGX-111 parent model.

efficacy.model: Idua-/- mouse, ZFN albumin-locus IDUA insertion
efficacy.note: Mouse editing corrected GAG storage and prevented neurobehavioral deficits.
efficacy.quote: A corrective copy of the IDUA gene is inserted at the albumin locus in hepatocytes, leading to sustained enzyme expression, secretion from the liver into circulation, and subsequent uptake systemically at levels sufficient for correction of metabolic disease

efficacy.magnitude_basis: brain storage reduction (mouse) vs DQ stabilization (patients)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; uncontrolled single-arm comparison with baseline; the registered primary outcome was adverse events.
efficacy.note: Developmental quotient and cortical grey matter stabilized over 52 weeks in cognitively impaired children.
efficacy.quote: The DQ, and the cortical grey matter volume of brain, were stabilized by valanafusp alpha treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. No efficacy primary or PoC gate existed (primary was safety); scored on the reported CNS outcome, so endpoint_role null and partial.

efficacy.model: Idua-/- mouse, lentiviral HSC gene therapy
efficacy.note: Urinary GAG normalized by 12 months in 4 of 5; cognition stable, growth normal, CSF GAG cleared.
efficacy.quote: Urinary glycosaminoglycan (GAG) excretion decreased steeply, reaching normal levels at 12 months in four of five patients who could be evaluated.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The efficacy primary does not exist (primaries were safety and blood IDUA); scored on GAG clearance and neurodevelopment, so endpoint_role null.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CNS storage correction (cat) vs neurodevelopmental trajectory
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor press release; few patients, some on ERT. Peer-reviewed single-patient IND report Wang 2026 agrees.
efficacy.model: MPS I cat and dog, intrathecal/intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA
efficacy.note: Children dosed with RGX-111 kept acquiring skills within 2 SD of normal, above untransplanted Hurler natural history.
efficacy.quote: Early assessments from the two patients under the age of six years old demonstrated continued skill acquisition within two standard deviations of the normative mean at last assessment on the BSID-III cognition, expressive language and fine motor subtests.
efficacy.judgement: Tier 5, model side Hinderer 2014. Primary was safety; scored on the neurodevelopmental read-out, endpoint_role null.

patient_trials.quote: His neurodevelopment is significantly above the natural history of untransplanted Hurler syndrome patients.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: urine heparan sulfate change at 24 months
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results; quote is the outcome definition; values read from the posted table. Patients on background ERT, a confound.
efficacy.model: Idua-/- mouse, ZFN albumin-locus IDUA insertion
efficacy.note: At 24 months urine heparan sulfate and total GAG did not fall in either cohort (+30.2 and +3.6 HS).
efficacy.quote: Change from baseline in total GAG, Dermatan Sulfate GAG, and Heparan Sulfate GAG measured in urine at Month 24
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me with Ou 2018. Primary was safety; scored on the registered urine GAG secondary, endpoint_role null. Background ERT blunts any GAG change.

safety.model: Rhesus monkey PK and chronic toxicology, AGT-181
safety.note: 6-month rhesus toxicology: HIR antibody's weak insulin agonism caused hypoglycemia at 30 mg/kg without dextrose.
safety.quote: The results show that the HIRMAb has weak insulin agonist activity and causes hypoglycemia at the high dose, 30 mg/kg, after intravenous infusion in normal saline.
safety.judgement: Named harm, on-target to the HIR antibody but specific to the protein modality.

safety.model: Rhesus monkey PK and chronic toxicology, AGT-181
safety.note: Transient hypoglycemia was a drug-related event in patients (6.4% incidence), as the monkeys predicted.
safety.quote: Drug related adverse events included infusion related reactions, with an incidence of 1.7%, and transient hypoglycemia, with an incidence of 6.4%.
safety.judgement: Paired by me. Monkeys showed it only at 30 mg/kg in saline; patients had it at up to 6 mg/kg, so the harm matched in kind, partial on dose.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. RGX-111 patients reported only mild TEAEs (press release 2022, Wang 2026); no sensory nerve testing found in either.
safety.model: Rhesus macaque GLP toxicology, intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA
safety.note: GLP macaque study: CSF pleocytosis and asymptomatic dorsal root ganglion degeneration; flagged for monitoring.
safety.quote: All vector-treated animals showed a dose-dependent mononuclear pleocytosis in the cerebrospinal fluid and minimal to moderate asymptomatic degeneration of dorsal root ganglia neurons and associated axons.
safety.reason: DRG lesion not measured in patients
safety.judgement: The predicted harm was histological and asymptomatic; no source reports sensory nerve conduction or DRG readouts in RGX-111 patients, so not compared rather than contradicted.

safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC author manuscript via Firecrawl).
safety.quote: we observed that immune-mediated toxicity was dose dependent, the peak of the immune response occurred 3 weeks after vector administration, presented with focal motor symptoms likely due to high transduction of spinal motor neurons, and was accompanied by CSF pleocytosis.
safety.note: Non-tolerized dogs showed dose-dependent anti-hIDUA immune toxicity with pleocytosis; RGX-111 patients were immunosuppressed and pleocytosis was not reported.
safety.judgement: The authors said the dog response likely exaggerates humans; with protocol immunosuppression the press release's 'no drug-related SAEs' cannot test the prediction.
safety.model: MPS I dogs tolerized to human IDUA, intracisternal AAV9-hIDUA (clinical candidate vector)

safety.quote: Overall, the results obtained in these studies provided robust evidence to support the safety and tolerability of high-efficiency LV-mediated gene transfer and above-normal IDUA enzyme expression in both murine and human HSPCs and their in vivo progeny.
safety.note: GLP toxicology, tumorigenicity and integration-site studies predicted above-normal IDUA expression would be tolerated without vector-related toxicity.
safety.model: NSG mice engrafted with human (incl. MPS I patient) HSPCs transduced with clinical-grade IDUA lentiviral vector; GLP tox/biodistribution

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; median follow-up 2.1 years limits insertional-oncogenesis assessment.
safety.quote: At a median follow-up of 2.10 years, the procedure had a safety profile similar to that known for autologous hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.
safety.note: No harm beyond autologous transplant in eight children at 2.1 years, as the xenograft toxicology predicted.
safety.judgement: Predicted absence of overexpression/vector toxicity scored as a stated prediction that held; follow-up is short for clonal events.
safety.model: NSG mice engrafted with human (incl. MPS I patient) HSPCs transduced with clinical-grade IDUA lentiviral vector; GLP tox/biodistribution
